heading: Frequently asked questions
description: The honest answers to what teams ask before they put Helix in front of their codebase.

items.question: What exactly does Helix do?
items.answer: Helix takes a single natural-language intent and breaks it into small, atomic units of work. Each unit has its own acceptance criteria, dependency map, and verification gate (types, tests, lint). Units execute in dependency order and surface as reviewable PRs instead of one sprawling diff.

items.question: How does Helix verify the agent's output?
items.answer: Each atomic unit is checked against the rest of your repo before it ships. Helix runs your type checker, your test suite, and your linter scoped to the unit's blast radius. If verification fails, the unit is re-tried or surfaced for human review — never silently merged.

items.question: Does Helix work with my existing codebase?
items.answer: Yes. Helix reads your repository the same way your senior engineer would — module boundaries, conventions, prior PRs. It does not require a greenfield project or a rewrite. You point it at a Git repo and a ticket, and it produces PRs that respect the code that's already there.

items.question: Why PRs instead of one big diff?
items.answer: Small PRs are easier to review, easier to revert, and easier to attribute. Helix's atomic work-breakdown exists so that an agent's output looks like the output of a thoughtful teammate, not a token firehose. Every PR has a clear scope, a clear description, and a clean revert path.

items.question: Which languages and frameworks are supported?
items.answer: Helix is language-agnostic at the orchestration layer. Out of the box it ships first-class support for TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, and Go — including their dominant test runners and linters. New languages plug in via a small adapter that exposes the project's verification commands.

items.question: How is Helix priced?
items.answer: Helix is free during the early-access period. There are no seat fees, no per-PR charges, and no usage caps while we collect feedback. When general availability lands, pricing will be based on units executed per month — predictable, with volume discounts for teams.

items.question: Where does my code run?
items.answer: Your code runs in isolated environments scoped to each unit. Helix never trains on your repository, never sends code to third-party model providers without an explicit provider list you control, and ships with audit logs for every run so security teams can review exactly what happened.

items.question: How do I get started?
items.answer: Clone the repository, point Helix at a ticket or a one-sentence feature description, and watch the first PRs land. The README has a five-minute quick start; the docs go deeper on adapter authoring, dependency graphs, and replays.
